PyTorch’s `Tensor.unfold` creates overlapping window views without initially copying data; reshaping into convolution batches may require materialization. Running a multilayer network over every length-W window still duplicates intermediate computation and activations. Analytical estimate for B sequences, T targets, D convolution layers, width C and kernel size k: full-sequence processing costs O(BTDkC²), versus O(BTWDkC²) for independent windows; dilation enlarges receptive field without increasing kernel taps. These estimates exclude backend workspaces and scoring. [Unfold documentation](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.Tensor.unfold.html), [tensor views](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/tensor_view.html), [Conv1d](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.Conv1d.html).

Chunking window batches bounds activation memory only when each chunk’s backward pass releases its graph. Accumulate appropriately normalized gradients and perform one optimizer step after all chunks; summing graph-connected losses before backward retains their activations. Chunking preserves the repeated arithmetic and adds launch overhead. Activation checkpointing offers another memory tradeoff through recomputation. These are implementation deductions, not measured throughput guarantees. [Checkpointing documentation](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/utils/checkpoint.html).

Exact truncated-context semantics require independently cropping each target’s history, left-padding it, applying the same network and taking its final-position output. For stride-one local convolutions, receptive field R=1+Σ(kℓ−1)dℓ. With W≥R, full-sequence outputs match independent windows when padding, normalization and other operations are compatible; with W<R, full-sequence hidden states can carry information from before each crop boundary. Merely masking the final output cannot remove that information. Preserve layerwise boundary padding, padding-token treatment and inference readout; sequence-wide normalization can also break equivalence. For strict crop semantics, chunked independent windows using one shared NextItNet remain the straightforward implementation, with potentially substantial training cost.
